quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What abilities does alcohol harm?
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms all the skills needed to drive safely. It affects judgment, reaction time, vision, reasoning, and concentration. Alcohol enters your bloodstream quickly and reaches your brain within minutes.

questions.question: This sign is a:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to special situations or hazards ahead.

questions.question: When you see angry drivers around you, you should:
questions.explanation: When drivers are angry, distance yourself physically and mentally from the situation. Do not make eye contact or use hand gestures that could provoke them. Slow down, move over, or do whatever you safely can to avoid danger.

questions.question: Drivers who drink alcohol before driving:

options.text: Always know they are taking risks.
Cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
Drive better because they are more careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant that harms judgment, vision, concentration, understanding, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: When you see a green traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through, unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive through, unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles still in the intersection. You can proceed, but drive at a speed that lets you stop if the light changes before you reach it.

questions.question: After an accident, a driver must:

options.text: Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.

questions.explanation: After an accident, stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes—you could be hit by another car. Turn off engines in wrecked vehicles.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no train in sight, you must stop if:
questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if red lights are flashing, a gate is lowered, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you, or a train is visible or close. If you are unsure, stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: On major highways, you should:

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected hazards. To avoid highway hypnosis, do not focus on any one thing for more than a few seconds.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving but harms judgment.
It harms both driving and judgment.
It harms driving but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms skills needed for safe driving, including reaction time and vision. It also affects your judgment of speed and distance, lowers your caution, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: You miss your freeway exit. What should you do?

options.text: Make a U-turn across the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to your exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next one. Do not stop, back up, or cross the median on a highway. Do not swerve across lanes at the last second. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Is smoking while driving a distraction?

options.text: No, it does not affect driving.
No, it helps you stay alert.
No, it is not a distraction.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving distracts you. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving?

options.text: It slows your reflexes and reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: It slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and reduces your driving skills. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: Which of these can impair your driving?
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires you to be in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and drowsiness can all impair your driving.

questions.question: You are angry after a work incident. What should you do before driving?

options.text: Play the radio loudly to stop thinking about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to release your anger.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
Stop at a bar and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, calm down before driving. Driving while angry is dangerous and bad judgment for you and others on the road.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black text on a yellow background. This sign warns you that the right lane is ending or the road is narrowing.

questions.question: You hit a parked car with no one inside. What must you do?

options.text: You can drive away without stopping.
Find the owner or leave a written note about what happened.
You do not need to contact your insurance company.
You can leave the scene without leaving a note.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find the owner or leave a written note about what happened.
questions.explanation: You must stop and find the vehicle's owner or leave a written note. Include your full name, address, and a description of what happened.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left.

questions.question: What is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can harm an infant or small child, even at low speeds.
All passengers should use seat belts or child restraints.

questions.explanation: Always use your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce injury and death in crashes. Children 12 and under should sit in the back seat. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat if there is a front airbag.

questions.question: What is important to know about trucks?

options.text: They need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
They pass faster going downhill than smaller vehicles.
They turn with a smaller radius than smaller vehicles.
They pass faster going uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are large and heavy, they need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: What could cause you to crash?

options.text: Taking your eyes off the road.
Taking your hands off the wheel.
Taking your attention away from driving.

questions.explanation: Anything that takes your attention from driving, your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel is a distraction and increases your crash risk.

questions.question: When passing a large truck, what should you do?

options.text: Move back into your lane and slow down right away.
Give the truck plenty of space before moving back into your lane.
Move back into your lane whenever you want.
Move back into your lane when you are directly next to the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the truck plenty of space before moving back into your lane.
questions.explanation: Don't move back too quickly after passing a large truck. Look in your rearview mirror to see the entire front of the truck before changing lanes. Don't slow down. Trucks and buses need twice as much space to stop as other vehicles.

questions.question: You must always signal when:

options.text: Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area. Signals help other drivers know what you are doing and prevent accidents.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pull to the right side of the road and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, make a clear path and stop. Slow down and safely pull to the side of the road. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: Motorcycles on the road:

options.text: Have the same rights and responsibilities as larger vehicles.
Do not have to follow traffic rules.
Must always yield to larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have the same rights and responsibilities as larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are vehicles with the same rights and responsibilities as larger vehicles. Car and truck drivers must respect the rights of motorcyclists.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you change your vehicle's position. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors to make sure no one is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: To stay safe at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and proceed only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and proceed only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Look and listen for trains from both directions before crossing. Watch for signals warning of a train. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When approaching a T intersection, you should:

options.text: Yield the right-of-way to traffic on the crossing road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to traffic on the crossing road.
questions.explanation: At a T intersection, if you are on the street that ends, you must stop and yield to vehicles on the crossing road. Only go when it is safe.

questions.question: Road rage and aggressive driving can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: Road rage happens more often as roads get busier. To prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.
